title: No News Is News: Do Markets Underreact to Nothing?

rival_explanations: event-time variation in systematic risk (Fama-French factors) compensates for the return pattern
event-time variation in downside risk drives the return pattern
event-time variation in idiosyncratic risk drives the return pattern
event-time variation in market frictions and asymmetric information (selling pressure, liquidity) drives the return pattern
last day / delisting return frictions generate the return pattern

context.industry_setting: cross-industry (mergers of publicly traded U.S. firms, spanning all sectors with no focal industry)
context.country_region: United States (U.S. targets for cash mergers; U.S. targets and acquirers for equity mergers)
context.sample_description: Mergers combining the Mitchell-Pulvino (MP) dataset (1970-2005) and the Thomson One / SDC (TO) dataset (1985-2010); restricted to all cash-financed or all equity-financed simple one-step mergers without a known expiration date, U.S. targets (and acquirers for equity deals) matched to CRSP returns, excluding tender offers, deals competing with a prior bid in the past three years, and deals where the target price exceeds the offer price after announcement

data_sources.name: Center for Research in Security Prices (CRSP)

dv.measure: theta captures the degree of underreaction from beliefs h_hat(t)=(1-theta)h_bar + theta*h(t); estimated from data on hazards and returns and tested against theta=1 (full rationality)

key_ivs.measure: estimated true hazard rates h(t) and average hazard rate h_bar

dv.measure: model-implied beliefs h_hat(t) chosen so that model-implied returns match observed average return in each event week, compared to estimated true hazard rates via the Cramer-Von Mises test (critical values from Klein and Moeschberger 2003)
